name: Ginnethon
overview: Ginnethon was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as an Aaronic priest. He is specifically mentioned in the sealed document of Nehemiah 10:1-27, highlighting his role among the priestly leaders during the post-exilic period. His priestly service underscores his importance in maintaining the covenantal worship of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Ginnethon appears in Nehemiah 10:6, with a variant spelling Ginnethoi found in Nehemiah 12:4. There is no recorded meaning of the name, and it was not given by God, indicating it was a common proper name without explicit divine origin or symbolic meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Meshullam as Ginnethon's father, as inferred from Nehemiah 12:16. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are recorded for Ginnethon in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ginnethon's significance lies in his role as an Aaronic priest during a critical period of Israel's restoration after exile. His inclusion in the covenantal oath document in Nehemiah 10 signifies his commitment to uphold the law and priestly duties. This positions him as a faithful leader dedicated to the spiritual renewal of the community under God's covenant.
